headline: Histology and host transcriptomes used to infer unmeasured spatial molecular layers
label: Cross Modal Spatial Omics Inference
summary: New preprints predict spatial protein, transcriptome and pathogen maps from histology or host RNA, alongside missing-modality survival models.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inferring an unmeasured spatial layer from measured modalities. MorphoProt predicts spatial protein abundance via RNA-guided cross-attention over multiscale histology and tissue neighborhoods, outperforming RNA-only baselines. PatHoST uses weak supervision to reconstruct pathogen spatial distributions from host spatial transcriptomes, with M. abscessus benchmarking. From histology, a multi-scale graph neural network predicts bulk, spatial and single-cell transcriptomics from whole-slide images. HistoTx early-fuses H&E patches with transcript tokens at arbitrary resolution under continued self-supervised training. TRACER adds a twin-contrastive graph autoencoder for rare and fine-grained spatial domain identification. A secondary strand addresses cancer survival. CMVAE contrastively aligns single-omic latents to survival. GOTSurv applies unbalanced optimal transport to TCGA cross-sectional data to derive risk strata and progression routes. DMG-PoE fuses incomplete multi-omics through uncertainty-aware product-of-experts. What is new is conditioning histology-based inference on a co-measured molecular layer rather than predicting from images alone.
